arxiv-2101-10162.title: Solving a Multi-resource Partial-ordering Flexible Variant of the Job-shop Scheduling Problem with Hybrid ASP
arxiv-2101-10162.creator: Giulia Francescutto, Konstantin Schekotihin, Mohammed M. S. El-Kholany
arxiv-2101-10162.description: Abstract Many complex activities of production cycles, such as quality control or fault analysis, require highly experienced specialists to perform various operations on (semi)finished products using different tools. In practical scenarios, the selection of a next operation is complicated, since each expert has only a local view on the total set of operations to be performed.

arxiv-2105-07979.title: Permutations designs, projective planes, and transitive sets of permutations Thanks: This research is supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (12071001, 61672036), Excellent Youth Foundation of Natural Science Foundation of Anhui Province (1808085J20), the Academic Fund for Outstan
arxiv-2105-07979.creator: Minjia Shi, XiaoXiao Li, Patrick Solé
arxiv-2105-07979.description: Abstract A notion of t t -designs in the symmetric group on n n letters, called permutation designs in this paper, was introduced by Godsil in 1988. In particular t t -transitive sets of permutations form a t t -design in that sense.

arxiv-2109-12410.title: Limits and colimits, generators and relations of partial groups
arxiv-2109-12410.creator: Edoardo Salati
arxiv-2109-12410.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Edoardo Salati. We analyse limits and colimits in the category P ​ a ​ r ​ t Part of partial groups, algebraic structures introduced by A. We will prove that P ​ a ​ r ​ t Part is both complete and cocomplete and, in addition, that the full subcategory of finite partial groups is both finitely complete and finitely cocomplete. Cocompleteness is then used in order to define quotients of partial groups.

arxiv-2303-14513.title: Shadows in dyonic Kerr-Sen black holes
arxiv-2303-14513.creator: Soumya Jana, Sayan Kar
arxiv-2303-14513.description: Abstract Black holes with dyonic charges in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion supergravity theory are revisited in the context of black hole shadows. We consider static as well as rotating (namely the dyonic Kerr-Sen) black holes. The matter stress-energy tensor components, sourced by the Maxwell, axion and dilaton fields satisfy the standard energy conditions.

arxiv-2308-11508.title: Rogue peakon, well-posedness, ill-posedness and blow-up phenomenon for an integrable Camassa-Holm type equation Thanks: Corresponding author
arxiv-2308-11508.creator: Mingxuan Zhu
arxiv-2308-11508.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mingxuan Zhu. In this paper, we study an integrable Camassa-Holm (CH) type equation with quadratic nonlinearity. The CH type equation is shown integrable through a Lax pair, and particularly the equation is found to possess a new kind of peaked soliton (peakon) solution - called rogue peakon , that is given in a rational form with some logarithmic function, but not a regular traveling wave. We also provide multi-rogue peakon solutions.

arxiv-2405-13175.title: FV8: A Forced Execution JavaScript Engine for Detecting Evasive Techniques
arxiv-2405-13175.creator: Nikolaos Pantelaios, Alexandros Kapravelos
arxiv-2405-13175.description: Abstract Evasion techniques allow malicious code to never be observed. This impacts significantly the detection capabilities of tools that rely on either dynamic or static analysis, as they never get to process the malicious code. The dynamic nature of JavaScript, where code is often injected dynamically, makes evasions particularly effective.

arxiv-2406-04833.title: A Remark on the Expressivity of Asynchronous TeamLTL and HyperLTL
arxiv-2406-04833.creator: Juha Kontinen, Max Sandström✉, Jonni Virtema
arxiv-2406-04833.description: Abstract Linear temporal logic (LTL) is used in system verification to write formal specifications for reactive systems. However, some relevant properties, e.g. non-inference in information flow security, cannot be expressed in LTL. A class of such properties that has recently received ample attention is known as hyperproperties.

arxiv-2409-01525.title: Bridging the Gap Between Central and Local Decision-Making: The Efficacy of Collaborative Equilibria in Altruistic Congestion Games
arxiv-2409-01525.creator: Bryce L. Ferguson, Dario Paccagnan, Bary S. R. Pradelski, and Jason R. Marden
arxiv-2409-01525.description: Abstract Congestion games are popular models often used to study the system-level inefficiencies caused by selfish agents, typically measured by the price of anarchy. One may expect that aligning the agents’ preferences with the system-level objective–altruistic behavior–would improve efficiency, but recent works have shown that altruism can lead to more significant inefficiency than selfishness in congestion games.

arxiv-2503-20952.title: TS-Inverse: A Gradient Inversion Attack Tailored for Federated Time Series Forecasting Models Thanks: This research was partially supported by the SNSF project, Priv-GSyn (grant number 200021E_229204), and the Advanced Computing Engineering (ACE) Department at TNO.
arxiv-2503-20952.creator: Anonymous Authors, Caspar Meijer 1 2, Jiyue Huang 1, Shreshtha Sharma 2, Elena Lazovik 2, Lydia Y. Chen 1 3
arxiv-2503-20952.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) for time series forecasting (TSF) enables clients with privacy-sensitive time series (TS) data to collaboratively learn accurate forecasting models, for example, in energy load prediction. Unfortunately, privacy risks in FL persist, as servers can potentially reconstruct clients’ training data through gradient inversion attacks (GIA).

arxiv-2602-21337.title: A Benchmark to Assess Common Ground in Human-AI Collaboration
arxiv-2602-21337.creator: Christian Poelitz a , Finale Doshi-Velez b and Siân Lindley a
arxiv-2602-21337.description: Abstract AI is becoming increasingly integrated into everyday life, both in professional work environments and in leisure and entertainment contexts. This integration requires AI to move beyond acting as an assistant for informational or transactional tasks toward a genuine collaborative partner.

pmc-10672029.creator: João Fontes Pereira, Rosana Costa, Miguel Nunes Vasques, Filomena Salazar, José Manuel Mendes, Marco Infante da Câmara, Lauren Bohner, Marcel Hanisch
pmc-10672029.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Osseodensification is an innovative method of preparing the implant osteotomy using drills that promote bone self-compaction. The main objective of this technique is to promote peri-implant bone densification and compaction of autologous bone and to increase the primary stability of the implant due to the viscoelastic characteristics of the alveolar bone using Densah® burs in a counterclockwise direction at a speed of 800 to 1500 rpm.

pmc-11492712.title: Elevated peripheral inflammation is associated with choroid plexus enlargement in independent sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis cohorts
pmc-11492712.creator: Sujuan Sun, Yujing Chen, Yan Yun, Bing Zhao, Qingguo Ren, Xiaohan Sun, Xiangshui Meng, Chuanzhu Yan, Pengfei Lin, Shuangwu Liu
pmc-11492712.description: BackgroundUsing neuroimaging techniques, growing evidence has suggested that the choroid plexus (CP) volume is enlarged in multiple neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Notably, the CP has been suggested to play an important role in inflammation-induced CNS damage under disease conditions.

pmc-11689769.title: DEMENTIA AND LONG-RUN CHANGES IN FINANCIAL HEALTH AMONG US HOUSEHOLDS
pmc-11689769.creator: Jing Li, Amy Kelley, Kathleen McGarry, Lauren Nicholas, Jonathan Skinner
pmc-11689769.description: We use two decades of the U.S. Health and Retirement Study data to compare long-run trajectories in household finances between individuals who eventually developed dementia and those who did not. In prior work, we find large and steady divergence in household wealth that starts 6-8 years prior to dementia onset.

pmc-11850398.title: Stewardship and social justice: implications of using the precautionary principle to justify burdensome antimicrobial stewardship measures
pmc-11850398.creator: Tess Johnson
pmc-11850398.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Antimicrobial resistance has been termed a ‘silent pandemic’, a ‘hidden killer.’ This language might indicate a threat of significant future harm to humans, animals, and the environment from resistant microbes. If that harm is uncertain but serious, the precautionary principle might apply to the issue, and might require taking ‘precautionary measures’ to avert the threat of antimicrobial resistance, including stewardship interventions like antibiotic prescription caps, bans on certain uses in farming sectors, and eliminating over-the-counter uses of antibiotics.

Thus, identifying those immunogenic epitopes driving T-cell activation conforms a fundamental goal for antigen-based immunotherapies. T-cell antigen discovery is challenged by immense epitope landscapes, unfeasible to screen ad hoc experimentally due to the high cost and low throughput of immunogenicity validations.
